TLS certificates

There are two certificates in this system and they are not the same thing: one protects the panel in your browser, and one protects the panel's connection to each node.

The panel's certificate

The installer offers five choices: Let's Encrypt for a domain, Let's Encrypt for the server's public IPv4 (short-lived), a custom pair, a self-signed pair, or no TLS. The Let's Encrypt options use the panel's built-in ACME client — nothing else has to be installed on the host.

Point the domain (or the IP) at this server and leave port 80 reachable: the client answers the HTTP-01 challenge on a listener that exists only while it runs. Issue or replace a certificate at any time with:

The panel stores the pair at DATA_DIR/tls (or the TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile you declare) and renews it automatically. The check runs daily; the window is a third of the certificate's lifetime, capped at 30 days, so a 90-day domain certificate renews around day 60 and a short-lived IP certificate renews with about two days left. The server reloads the pair on the next handshake, so a renewal is served without a restart.

The ACME account key lives at DATA_DIR/tls/acme-account.pem. Set AcmeDirectoryUrl to the Let's Encrypt staging directory to test without using production quota.

Use your own certificate

A certificate from certbot, acme.sh or your CA still works:

Point TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile at the pair, or leave them unset to use DATA_DIR/tls. The panel reloads a renewed pair on the next handshake; restart only when the panel has to switch between HTTP and HTTPS.

The node's certificate

The node's sync API also serves TLS. The installer never offers plain HTTP — the API key travels in a header on every request. The panel verifies that certificate strictly first, and warns once per node when a self-signed fallback is forced.

The node's OpenVPN server certificate is a separate thing. The node generates and manages it; ovnode tls on the node shows and replaces it, and the panel reports its expiry through the sync API.

Watching for expiry

WhereWhat to look at
Panel, via ovmanager tlsInstalled certificate, source and expiry; built-in ACME renews it automatically
Node, via ovnode tls statusNode sync API certificate (self-signed or Let's Encrypt) and remaining validity
Node, via ovnode statusOpenVPN server certificate expiry, refreshed per probe

TLS is terminated by the panel

The panel serves HTTPS itself. There is no reverse-proxy mode: forwarded headers are not trusted, the client IP is the peer address, and HSTS is emitted only on a real TLS connection. Point DNS at the panel and use TlsCertFile/TlsKeyFile (or the installer's TLS step) for the certificate.
